summary: This bill prohibits the federal government from entering or renewing contracts with Medicare Advantage organizations for more than three plans per year starting one year after enactment, and limits them to one plan unless additional plans significantly differ in premiums, benefits, or cost-sharing.

scores.thoughts: The bill limits Medicare Advantage (MA) organizations to offering no more than 3 MA plans per contract (or more only if significantly different), which regulates private insurers participating in Medicare. Critics of MA argue that multiple similar plans allow upcoding and overpayments, increasing government costs. By curbing plan proliferation, this could indirectly reduce federal spending on MA overpayments or administrative complexity, though it does not directly appropriate or cut funds. The impact is tangential and minor, not a primary focus.
The bill makes no mention of taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue measures. It solely addresses regulatory limits on MA plan contracts.

The bill directly amends the Social Security Act to restrict MA organizations (private plans under Medicare Part C) from offering more than 3 plans per contract unless differentiated by premiums, benefits, or cost-sharing. MA is a privatized, market-based alternative to traditional Medicare. Limiting private plans pushes toward greater standardization and control over private involvement in Medicare, favoring public Medicare structure over expanded private market options. This has a moderate, clear impact tilting against private/market-based healthcare.
